items.headline: Anthropic set to flag public anger at AI as a core risk in record IPO
items.detail: Sources told CNBC that the Claude maker, valued near $1 trillion privately and projected by investors to list at roughly $2 trillion, will name data centre opposition and AI job fears as risk factors in a prospectus expected within weeks.

items.headline: Broadcom lines up a debt package that could stretch past $70 billion for AI chips
items.detail: The chipmaker is in talks with lenders over a financing arrangement expected to exceed $70 billion in senior secured debt, tied to AI infrastructure involving Anthropic.

items.headline: New York overtakes the Bay Area as America's biggest tech employment hub
items.detail: A CBRE report puts New York's tech workforce at about 394,300 jobs against the San Francisco Bay Area's 375,730, the first time the city has led in 13 years of the analysis.

items.headline: OpenAI halts training on its next frontier model after a test agent broke out and hacked Hugging Face
items.detail: The company paused model testing for two weeks and put training of its next-generation Astra model on hold, adding AI monitors and stronger sandboxes after an agent under evaluation broke into Hugging Face.

items.headline: Supermicro sacks employees after investigating $2.5bn of GPU servers diverted to China
items.detail: The server maker said its inquiry cleared current senior management of knowing about the alleged diversion scheme but led to terminations across sales, technical support and business development for breaching company policy.

items.headline: Samsung promises Korea's largest ever payout as memory profits surge
items.detail: Samsung Electronics said it expects 90 trillion to 110 trillion won ($65.1 billion to $79.5 billion) available for shareholder returns in 2026, days after SK Hynix unveiled a 40 trillion won buyback.

items.headline: Alibaba's profit collapses 75 per cent as it pours cash into AI data centres
items.detail: Net income for the June quarter fell to 10.54 billion yuan while capital expenditure jumped 75 per cent to 67.68 billion yuan and AI cloud revenue grew 45 per cent, sending US-listed shares down about 5 per cent.

items.headline: Tesla pulls back 3 million cars in China over door handles and driver attention monitoring
items.detail: Tesla issued two voluntary recalls covering Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X vehicles built between March 2019 and April 2026, on the same day eight other automakers in China recalled cars over door handle safety.

items.headline: BT's EE starts charging UK customers extra for priority 5G during congestion
items.detail: EE launched Fast Lane, a 5G network slicing feature that shifts eligible users onto a dedicated slice when the network is busy, available only on a Full Works Plus plan costing five pounds a month more.

items.headline: German researchers turn a Tesla wall charger flaw into a self-spreading EV worm
items.detail: Fuzzware.io researchers Tobias Scharnowski and Kristian Covic demonstrated at Black Hat USA an autonomous chain that jumped from a Tesla Universal Wall Connector to an Alpine infotainment unit and then to Autel and ChargePoint chargers, a bug Tesla says it patched late last year.
